He directly set anti-corruption priorities and deadlines, while the Party rapidly created steering committees nationwide and disciplined senior officials. His China diplomacy also produced concrete tactical gains while preserving room for other relationships. These achievements show more than rhetoric or inherited state capacity. However, delivery was uneven. Independent citizen and business surveys found worsening local corruption-control and policy implementation in several areas, and stronger scrutiny made officials reluctant to approve projects and procurement. Economic growth was strong, but reopening, consumption, and exports were major causes, while recovery-program investment remained delayed and later audits identified persistent allocation and project-control weaknesses. Personnel decisions were formally collective, so the evidence does not establish that Trọng personally selected more capable replacements. The objectives' moral worth did not affect this execution score. The record supports a generally effective rating rather than 4–5 because ruler-attributed mobilization and diplomacy were concrete, but not 7.5 or higher because independently demonstrated outcomes,
